record.original_question: Given integers p > q >= 2 and m,n in N, determine the maximum number of 2pi-periodic limit cycles for Abel-type equations x' = A_m(t)x^p + B_n(t)x^q where A_m and B_n are trigonometric polynomials of degrees m and n, respectively.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Given two integer numbers p > q >= 2, and m, n in N, find the maximum number of 2pi periodic limit cycles for next family of Abel type differential equations dx/dt = Am(t)x^p + Bn(t)x^q, where Am and Bn are 2pi-trigonometric polynomials with respective degrees m and n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p and q be integers with p > q ≥ 2, and let m, n be positive integers. Consider the family of generalized Abel-type ordinary differential equations
   dx/dt = A(t) x^p + B(t) x^q,
where A(t) and B(t) are real-valued 2π-periodic trigonometric polynomials of degrees exactly m and n, respectively (i.e., A(t) = a_0 + Σ_{k=1}^{m}(a_k cos kt + b_k sin kt) with (a_m, b_m) ≠ (0,0), and similarly B(t) of degree n). A limit cycle is an isolated 2π-periodic solution x: ℝ → ℝ of this equation.

Determine, as a function H_{p,q}(m,n) of p, q, m, n, the maximum possible number of 2π-periodic limit cycles that such an equation can have, taken over all admissible choices of trigonometric polynomial coefficients A and B of the prescribed degrees.
artifact.category_tag: Abel differential equations and limit cycles
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of determining the maximum number of 2π-periodic limit cycles for generalized Abel equations x' = A(t)x^p + B(t)x^q with trigonometric polynomial coefficients of given degrees remains open. Only partial results exist: lower bounds (e.g., H_{3,2}(n,m) ≥ 2(n+m)-1), exact results in special cases such as linear trigonometric coefficients (giving 3 limit cycles for the classical p=3, q=2 case), and Chebyshev-type criteria providing upper bounds in restricted settings. Recent works (2023–2026) continue to address sub-cases rather than the full question.

status_evidence.title: Maximum number of limit cycles for Abel equation having coefficients with linear trigonometric functions
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the maximum number of limit cycles only in the special case of linear trigonometric coefficients, giving 3.
status_evidence.claim: Only a special case has been resolved; the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the Number of Limit Cycles in Generalized Abel Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies generalized Abel equations and provides bounds in restricted settings.
status_evidence.claim: General bound H_{p,q}(m,n) is not established; partial results only.

status_evidence.title: Rational solutions and limit cycles of polynomial and trigonometric Abel equations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses lower bounds such as H_{3,2}(n,m) ≥ 2(n+m)-1 and that no global bound is known for trigonometric coefficient case.
status_evidence.claim: The exact value of the maximum number of limit cycles is unknown in general.
